tasks.task: Pull every date and duty from a contract into one table

items.when: When you have a signed contract, memorandum of sale or addendum and need all dates in one table
When the contract is a scan, to pull the facts and check each against its page
When addenda have changed the dates, to get each clause's latest wording
Before the table is shared, to tie every date to its clause or mark it as not found

tasks.task: Build a deal deadline tracker back from the closing date

items.when: When the key dates are known and each needs an owner, a warning date and a status
When the target date looks hopeful, to correct it by how deals like this really went
When the tracker is drafted, to list the ways this deal could slip and what to change
When the agent wants the tracker as a clean spreadsheet with no invented rows

tasks.task: Write the document checklist for each stage of a sale

items.when: When a deal starts and you need what is due at each stage, from whom and by when
When the client is the buyer or seller, to see their documents and choices from offer to closing
When a loan is involved, to list missing loan documents, expiry dates and deadlines
At each stage gate, to mark every checklist line pass, fail or unknown with the proof

tasks.task: Run one deal from accepted offer to closed file

items.when: When an offer is accepted or a sale is agreed and every step must run in order
When the deal's dates must be tracked from day one
When each stage needs its own list of papers to collect and file
When tasks are buried in email threads, to get one action list with owners and dates

tasks.task: Write weekly updates for every party on a deal

items.when: Once a week per deal, or when a stage changes, so each party hears before they ask
When buyer, seller, lender and agent each need the same news at a different depth
When the update reads flat, to try a version that puts the reader's gain first
Before sending, to read the update as an anxious first-time buyer and list what they would ask
When an update buries the one thing the reader must do under a list of events

tasks.task: Build a reusable set of stage-by-stage update templates

items.when: When an agent wants templates for each stage in three parts: done, next, needed from you
Before the templates, to agree channels, update days and where decisions are recorded
When planning the whole message series, to compare three ways to pace it and pick one
When you need each stage mapped with what the buyer feels and where they get stuck
When templates are drafted, to cut trade words a first-time buyer will not know

tasks.task: Write a delay or bad news update

items.when: When a loan is late, an appraisal is low, a chain is delayed or a deadline is at risk
When you want a second, shorter version that leads with the loss and the next step
Before sending, to test every promise and date in the message against what you control
Before the phone call that follows, to plan calm questions and name the other side's worry

tasks.task: Check a message about wiring, deposits or bank details

items.when: When anyone on a deal gets an email, text or call about wiring money or new bank details
When every update must carry the standing wire safety line and the call-back rule
When the brokerage team needs a one-page rule sheet and a ten-minute drill
When the agent's own email domain is easy to fake and needs sender checks set up

tasks.task: Plan closing or completion day hour by hour

items.when: When the signing or completion time is set and the day must be planned back from it
When the day is planned, to list what could go wrong and add a fallback for each
The day before, to run the checklist line by line with proof for each item

tasks.task: Review every live deal on Monday and flag the ones at risk

items.when: When an agent has several live deals and wants what is due, at risk and owed an update
Before the review, to find deals with missing fields, stale dates or the wrong stage
Each week, to see where deals wait longest and whether the trend is getting worse
After the review, to give the broker one page on done, stuck and needed

tasks.task: Build a UK sale progression chase list

items.when: When an agent in England or Wales has many sales agreed and needs who to chase for what
When each chase needs a follow-up draft linked to its task and thread
When it is the third chase to a slow solicitor and the draft has turned sharp

tasks.task: Chase missing documents and overdue tasks

items.when: When tasks are due, to draft a follow-up for each with the missing facts marked
When several papers are missing or out of date, to draft one request per owner
Before chasing, to see exactly which documents this stage still needs
When replies are buried in a full inbox, to sort them and draft answers without sending

tasks.task: Summarise a contract or addendum in plain words

items.when: When a client wants a two-minute read of what they owe, what they get and the risky parts
When an addendum arrives, to trace each change and write a plain summary for the broker
When a term looks unusual, to list the questions to take to the broker or lawyer
When the summary must end with the dates and duties in one table

tasks.task: Write a what-happens-next guide for buyers and sellers

items.when: When clients keep asking the same questions, to turn them into one clear page
When a term like escrow or exchange needs an everyday comparison and its limits
When the guide should be a handout checked page by page
When the guide is drafted, to read it as a first-time buyer and list what is still unclear
When the guide lists steps but never walks through what the buyer sees and feels each week

tasks.task: Reply to an anxious or upset client

items.when: Before replying, to read the message for urgency, worry and warning signs
When the client is angry, to answer the feeling, fix what you can and promise nothing false
When the facts are right but the tone is not, to try the same reply warmer or firmer
Before sending, to check the reply gives no legal view and no promise you cannot keep
When a reply defends the process and forgets how the delay looks from the client's side

tasks.task: Read scanned documents and check a file is complete

items.when: When papers arrive as scans or photos and the text must be read with page positions
When PDFs must be merged, split or checked with the original kept safe
When names, prices and dates in a scan must match the contract
When the broker audits files, to get an index, a gap list and owners for each gap
When the file is closing, to tick every stage's papers before it is archived

tasks.task: Design a tracker or workspace for many deals at once

items.when: Before building, to fix the columns every deal needs: date, duty, owner, status
When deals are entered by hand, to get dropdowns and checks that stop bad entries
When agents hand over new deals, to plan an intake form that collects what you need once
When the brokerage keeps deals in Notion and wants pages and records updated there
When deadline reminders should fire on their own from the tracker to email or calendar

tasks.task: Turn calls and email threads into owned actions

items.when: After a call with several parties, to get actions with owners, dates and follow-up drafts
When rough call notes need short minutes with decisions and open questions
When calls should be transcribed live so nothing agreed is lost

tasks.task: Write the coordinator's procedure and cover handover

items.when: When the way deals are run lives in one head and needs a written procedure
When someone new takes over, to build a procedure and exception guide from a real deal
When the coordinator is away, to give the cover person each deal's tasks and who to call
When one deal moves to another person and they must run it from day one

tasks.task: Find why deals keep missing deadlines

items.when: When the same stage slips on deal after deal, to map the delay and its cause from records
When the same mistake repeats, to turn the misses into a one-page checklist and test it
After a hard deal closes, to note what to repeat and what to change

tasks.task: Close the file and follow up after completion

items.when: When the deal completes and the file must be closed with every paper in place
When the agent wants a thank-you note and a plan to stay in touch
When the thank-you should name one true, specific thing and ask for nothing
When the agent wants a review, to ask with three easy questions and one follow-up
Before the messages go, to keep them short and free of sales talk

always.when: When any message states a date, a duty or a sum, to tie it to the contract or cut it
Before any update goes out, to catch a wrong name, address, date or amount

helpers.when: When the brokerage needs its file rules checked against state, anti-money-laundering or data rules
When the job is mostly diary, inbox and booking inspections, surveys and signings
When the tracker must be built as a real workbook with date formulas and warnings
When reminders and updates should send themselves from the tracker
When the home is tenanted and notices, access and deposits must be handled before completion
When a brokerage needs a shared inbox answered every day across many deals

No library item covers title, escrow, earnest money, mortgage offers or searches in plain words for buyers
